answer: An agent economy can resist sybil farms by metering admission through a scarce wharf: a new identity gains almost no vote until it posts a slashable deposit and completes unique, non-replayable useful work that peers can audit. Influence then opens with a prism pace, only after several independent attesters record the same crystal of that work fingerprint. Clones collapse together when fingerprints collide, so minting a thousand voters costs a thousand deposits and a thousand distinct work streams, and a cheap majority cannot break even.
